svg.title: kS: volts to break free from friction
svg.desc: Animated. Left, two graphs drawn left to right: volts slowly rise from zero, and the wheel's speed stays at zero all the while the volts are below a dashed line marked kS, in a shaded band labeled 'nothing happens'. When the volts pass kS it breaks free and the speed rises; when the volts fall back below kS it stops again. Right, a wheel on carpet that stays still, then turns while the volts are above kS. Bearings, gears and carpet grip hold it back; kS is the voltage that just overcomes them. It points the way you want to go and does not depend on speed. A module needing much more kS than the others is binding.
svg.text: kS: volts to break free from friction
Volts it takes just to get the mechanism moving. Below kS nothing happens.
kS is the voltage that just overcomes them. It points the way you want to
go and does not depend on speed. A module needing much more kS than
the others is binding: a rubbing wheel, debris, or a misaligned pinion.
